title: Basic Sewing Skills
subtitle: Every stitch is a choice about strength.
objectives: Name the main hand stitches and their uses
Choose a stitch for a given job
Thread a needle and finish off securely

cards.title: A stitch is a choice about strength
cards.text: There is no single way to sew. Each stitch is strong or weak on purpose, and picking the wrong one is why a repair fails.

cards.title: Strong, weak, and deliberately temporary
cards.text: Three categories cover the whole set.
points: **Backstitch** — the strongest hand stitch.
**Running stitch** — fast and weak.
**Basting** — long, loose, meant to be removed.
**Hemming and overcast** — finishing an edge, not joining.

cards.title: Six buttons
cards.text: Tap each stitch. The second line is how much it will hold.

question.text: Which stitch would you use on a seam that has to hold?
question.explain: Each stitch doubles back on the last.

cards.title: A stitch designed to be weak
cards.text: This is the one that sounds pointless and is not.
points: **It holds two pieces still** while you sew properly.
**Pins slip and stab.** Basting does not.
**Long, loose and in a contrasting thread** so you can find it.
**Then you pull it out.** That was always the plan.

question.explain: It is meant to come out.

cards.title: Four things people skip
cards.text: A button sewn flat against the cloth will not fasten.
points: **Leave slack** for the thickness of the buttonhole layer.
**Build a shank** — a few wraps of thread under the button.
**Six passes is plenty.** Twenty makes it bulky, not stronger.
**Knot underneath**, where it will not be rubbed.

cards.title: Repair is cheaper than replacement
cards.text: Gear fails at the stitching long before the material gives up.
points: **Glove seams and bag straps** go first.
**A backstitched repair** lasts another season.
**Sewing is a cheap skill** with an expensive payoff.
**Nobody in a gym throws away a bag** over one seam.

cards.title: Four stitches, four strengths
cards.alt: Four rows of hand stitching on hooped fabric: running, backstitch, long basting and overcast along an edge
cards.text: Running, backstitch, basting, overcast. Find the one that is meant to come out.

question.text: Which stitch is designed to be removed again?
question.explain: Long, loose and in a contrasting thread so you can find it.

cards.title: A stitch is a mechanical fastener
cards.text: Think of it as thread doing what a screw does.
points: **A running stitch is one screw** every few centimetres.
**A backstitch overlaps**, so load is shared.
**Load is spread over more points.**
**Same reason bolts go in pairs.**

cards.title: Finish off or it unravels
cards.text: The last step is the one that decides whether any of it held.
points: **Three small stitches in the same place**, then knot.
**Do not rely on one knot.**
**An unfinished seam undoes itself** from the end.
**Saving is part of the work.**

cards.title: What to remember
points: Backstitch is strongest; running stitch is fast and weak.
Basting is deliberately weak and designed to be removed.
Hemming and overcast finish an edge rather than join.
Buttons need slack, a shank, and a knot underneath.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 9 TLE. Stitches are introduced by how much they hold rather than by name, which makes the set learnable as three categories: strong, fast-and-weak, and deliberately temporary. Basting gets its own card because a stitch designed to be weak sounds pointless until the reason is given, and because pins slipping is a real problem he will meet. The button card lists the four things people skip, with the one that matters most — slack for the buttonhole layer — first. The teardown lens treats a stitch as a mechanical fastener and a backstitch as overlapping load paths, which is both accurate and the framing most likely to land.
discussion: Ask which stitch he would use and why that one.
Ask why basting exists at all.
Ask what happens to a button sewn flat.
Ask how a seam is finished off.
extension: Have him sew a button on properly, with a shank, and test it in a buttonhole.
Have him repair one real thing — a strap, a hem, a seam.
misconceptions: "One stitch is as good as another." Strength is the whole choice.
"Basting is a waste of time." Pins slip; basting does not.
"More thread means a stronger button." Six passes is plenty.
